neighbours.label: future modal ' will' after a subject making a generic prediction or attribution ('experts will tell you', 'critics will argue')
fire: Ask around and most mechanics will tell you that synthetic oil is worth it.
As any gardener will tell you, tomatoes need plenty of sun.
Critics will argue that the plan costs far too much money.
Historians will point out that the treaty was signed under pressure.
Most teachers will agree that homework alone does not build skills.
As nutritionists will tell you, breakfast is not a magic meal.
Skeptics will say that the results have not been replicated yet.
Any good lawyer will tell you to read the contract twice.
quiet: Ask around and most mechanics told me that synthetic oil is worth it.
As any gardener knows, tomatoes need plenty of sun.
Critics have argued that the plan costs far too much money.
The historian's will left his papers to the national archive.
Most teachers agree that homework alone does not build skills.
As nutritionists often say, breakfast is not a magic meal.
She lacked the will to keep arguing with the skeptics.
Any good lawyer knows to read the contract twice.

notes: Probe: '... will tell you' / 'will point out' 0.73-0.76; noun will (testament, willpower) <0.01; 'would tell you' 0.26 (peak on tell); 'I will try' only 0.06, so the pole prefers will followed by a speech/opinion verb. Opposite pole is ' would'.
